root_idea.summary: A hollowed or rounded cavity, indentation, or opening; the root centers on making or becoming concave.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from hollowing and leaving impressions to pitting, peeling, uprooting, the opening of an egg, and related objects or measures.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is presented as the normalized nominal citation قَابٌ.

senses.definition: The portion of a bow between the handgrip and its curved extremity; hence, the measure or distance of a bow. In the Quranic expression, the distance of two bows or two bow-portions, or nearer.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَى to express a bow-based measure of nearness or distance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig or make a round, hollow cavity in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive verbal use, especially with the ground or earth as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to break its eggs apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with eggs as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of skin, to become pitted or marked with small hollows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use describing the skin's surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach or draw near; also, in a contrary attested usage, to flee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two directions are reported as contrasting lexical uses rather than as one combined action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make impressions, marks, or traces in the ground by treading or alighting, including indications at watering places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative/intensive Form II use involving footprints, landing, or similar marks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of mange or scab, to make pits in a camel's skin, leaving the affected places bare of fur.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested construction describes the effect of mange or scab on the camel's skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become sullied with dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive Form II expression describing a person or thing becoming dust-covered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pull something out or up by the root; to eradicate or uproot it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II use of complete removal from the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become peeled or excoriated, especially in several or many places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V use describing peeling or loss of the outer surface in patches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place, to become stripped in parts of its trees and herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested use concerns vegetation being removed from portions of a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be pulled out or up by the root; to be eradicated or uprooted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or reflexive Form V use describing removal from the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the ground, to become hollowed out in a round form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form VII use describing a rounded hollow being formed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an egg, to break open and disclose the young bird; figuratively, to reveal or manifest an affair, case, or state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative use is explicitly modeled on an egg opening to disclose what is within.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choose, select, elect, or prefer someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form VIII use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young bird, especially in relation to its emergence from an egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for the bird in the egg-and-hatching vocabulary of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An egg, including an egg from which the young bird has emerged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is reported with both the young-bird and egg senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the proverb concerning an egg freed from its young bird, the state of separation from one's companion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative application comparing a person's separation from a companion to the separation of a young bird and an egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calamity or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hollows or pits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested examples concern hollows in the ground and pits in the head or skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Eggshells.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal plural use distinct from the egg or young-bird senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ringworm, tetter, or a spreading cutaneous eruption in which scabs peel from the skin and hair comes off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A name for the disease or eruption, with the stated peeling and hair-loss features.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who remains constantly in his abode and does not leave it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a person characterized by staying at home.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fond of, or addicted to, eating young birds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective derived in connection with قُوبٌ, young birds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An empty egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression قَائِبَةُ قُوبٍ denotes an egg emptied of the young bird within it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land on which rain has fallen and from which, as a consequence, trees formerly growing in some places have been carried away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive participial expression for land partly stripped of its former vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Peeled or excoriated; of a person, one whose scabs have peeled away leaving marks and hairless patches; of a serpent, one that has cast off its skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle is applied to peeled surfaces, persons with the described skin condition, and a serpent after shedding its skin.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Digging or making a round hollow.
Approaching and the contrary use of fleeing.
Making impressions and traces in ground.
Pitting camel skin through mange or scab.
A place stripped of trees and herbage.

Young bird, egg, and the associated separation proverb.
Person who remains constantly at home.
Ringworm or related excoriating skin disease.
Person with peeled scabs and hairless marks.
Serpent that has shed its skin.

cautions: The Quranic group is tagged as a noun despite the surface spelling قَابَ; it is normalized here to the nominal citation قَابٌ, while the separate verbal قَابَ uses remain in the Classical meanings.
The Form VII Lane entry is headed اسقابت in the supplied transcription, while its body and cross-references support انقابت; the public citation follows the latter.
The verbal entry قَابَ records approaching and fleeing as contrary reported uses; these are retained together with that qualification rather than treated as one undifferentiated meaning.
